method: Full current-item reread against prior snapshot-validation findings, including all options, key, explanations and metadata. Original snapshots preserved. Each status manually reasoned; not blanket approval.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

sourceChecks.note: Explicitly advises stop ciprofloxacin, rest and call immediately for tendon pain; basis for safety addition to key.
Clarithromycin with simvastatin contraindicated because of increased myopathy/rhabdomyolysis risk; no dose instructions imported.
Opened current TMP-SMX label; interaction table explicitly identifies ACE inhibitors and hyperkalaemia. Revised item requires review, not autonomous electrolyte treatment.

items.assessment: Stable client with an immediately accessible sampling port permits ordered culture collection before antibiotics without waiting for culture results. Old drainage-bag urine is not a fresh diagnostic sample; the amended catheter context resolves applicability.

Susceptibility results plus response support team review for targeted effective coverage. Completing broad treatment on improvement alone, unnecessary overlap and a mandatory repeat culture are plausible stewardship errors; nurse does not independently switch agents.
Reaction details are correctly elicited, but the avoidance alternative declares missing clarification. Remove that cue while retaining the clinically meaningful overgeneralization.
issues: Reaction details are correctly elicited, but the avoidance alternative declares missing clarification. Remove that cue while retaining the clinically meaningful overgeneralization.

options: Remove the allergy because no written proof is available
Request an antibiotic from a different class because penicillins and cephalosporins are both beta-lactams
Ask what happened, when it occurred and what treatment was needed
Assume nausea and airway swelling carry the same risk
why: An undocumented history still needs investigation before removal.
A shared broad class does not establish identical allergy risk for every product; the reaction history and proposed antibiotic need assessment.
Reaction characteristics help the team assess the allergy and antibiotic plan.
Different reaction types require different clinical interpretation.

items.assessment: Improving respiratory/temperature trends and function at equal oxygen support indicate response. Antipyretic masking, somnolence or hypotension outweigh isolated apparently improved measures; both selected outcomes are supported.
New tinnitus and unsteadiness during gentamicin raise auditory/vestibular toxicity concern before confirmed hearing loss; prompt report and next-dose clarification avoid further unreviewed exposure.

Use the prior drug level to approve the next several doses

Intake comparison may inform hydration assessment but cannot establish current gentamicin clearance or safety with rising creatinine and falling urine output.
Reduced clearance can increase exposure after a previously acceptable level.

Reduce the rate until flushing settles, then restore the prescribed rate

issues: Painful spreading rash plus mucosal sores on TMP-SMX warrants urgent severe-reaction assessment. Remove the only qualifier in the antihistamine alternative.

The combined mucosal and painful skin findings require consideration of a severe drug reaction.

items.assessment: Calcium and antacid minerals can reduce doxycycline absorption; product-specific separation should be verified. Separating just one mineral source, adding food or an extra tablet does not reliably resolve the interaction. Foundation label fits.

Isolated orange urine during rifampin without other concerning symptoms can be expected discoloration. Explanation plus reporting precautions is better than assuming bleeding, dehydration or stopping therapy; foundation label fits.
New colour-perception and acuity changes during ethambutol warrant prompt assessment before more exposure. Absence of pain or the prospect of stronger glasses cannot exclude optic toxicity.
Neuropathy assessment plus the missed pyridoxine history is appropriate. Two alternatives explicitly advertise nonreview/nondisclosure rather than realistic competing care plans.
issues: Neuropathy assessment plus the missed pyridoxine history is appropriate. Two alternatives explicitly advertise nonreview/nondisclosure rather than realistic competing care plans.

options: Try wider footwear and reassess whether tingling improves over the coming week
Assess and report the tingling and missed pyridoxine
Restart pyridoxine and wait until the routine visit to mention symptoms
Provide foot-comfort advice and request an analgesic for the discomfort
why: A mechanical explanation should not postpone review of new bilateral tingling during isoniazid treatment with missed supplementation.
Possible isoniazid-related neuropathy and the supplementation plan require review.
Resuming supplementation does not remove the need to assess newly developed neuropathy.
Symptom management alone does not evaluate possible treatment-related neuropathy or address the missed pyridoxine plan.

items.assessment: Exploring tolerability/barriers and explaining prescribed combination therapy address contemplated partial TB treatment. Self-selecting one drug, saving doses for later and relying on symptom improvement risk failure/resistance.

Oral vancomycin delivers medicine to the intestinal treatment site; IV access convenience, equal-dose interchange and a mild-disease-only rule misconstrue route purpose. Foundation demand is explicit.

Oral nystatin requires prescribed mucosal contact rather than immediate swallowing/dilution/rinsing. Disappearing one patch does not independently define course completion; foundation label is appropriate.
Fluconazole/warfarin require interaction and anticoagulation follow-up. The dose-spacing alternative need not announce it is the only precaution.
issues: Fluconazole/warfarin require interaction and anticoagulation follow-up. The dose-spacing alternative need not announce it is the only precaution.

options: Advise extra vitamin K foods to offset the new drug
Interaction review and an appropriate anticoagulation-monitoring plan
Continue usual monitoring because both doses are standard
Take warfarin and fluconazole at different times of day to prevent the interaction
why: Unplanned dietary compensation makes anticoagulation less predictable.
Fluconazole can increase warfarin effect and bleeding risk.
Standard doses do not exclude a clinically significant interaction.

proposedChanges.stem: A client taking ramipril develops new weakness after starting trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Potassium rises from 4.4 to 5.8 mmol/L (reference 3.5–5.0), while creatinine is unchanged and the radial pulse is regular. What should the nurse do next?
options: Promptly report the potassium trend, weakness and medicines for rhythm and treatment review
Arrange a repeat potassium at tomorrow’s routine blood draw because creatinine is unchanged
Continue the current regimen while checking for an irregular pulse at routine observations
Separate ramipril and the antibiotic between morning and evening doses
why: The drug combination can raise potassium; a new elevation with weakness needs prompt clinical review despite a currently regular pulse.
Stable creatinine does not exclude a medication-related potassium rise or justify postponing assessment of new symptoms.
A regular palpable pulse does not exclude an important potassium disturbance or establish the regimen is safe to continue.
Dose spacing does not remove the potassium-retaining effects of trimethoprim and ACE inhibition.
proposedChanges.takeaway: Assess a new symptomatic potassium rise during interacting therapy even when creatinine and pulse appear stable.
proposedChanges.learningObjective: Integrate potassium trend, new symptoms and interacting therapy to select prompt treatment review.

Mix the antibiotic directly into the feed to dilute minerals

The interaction and nutrition requirements need coordinated management.
The appropriate interval depends on this product, the interaction and nutrition requirements; a schedule for another antibiotic is not interchangeable.
Mixing may worsen binding and make dosing incomplete.

why: Reduced vomiting would not remove the significance of fever and flank pain.
Routine delayed sampling is insufficient for newly systemic and flank symptoms that may indicate upper-tract infection.
Fever, flank pain and vomiting suggest progression beyond bladder-focused treatment.
Pain relief alone does not assess a possible upper urinary infection.

items.assessment: Following the individualized prescribed duration and promptly reporting severe adverse effects avoid symptom-based guessing, sharing, stockpiling and arbitrary restarting; wording permits the team to change treatment when warranted.

Reporting complications and observed aseptic connections support home-IV readiness. Flexible unprescribed rate changes, appearance-only identification and assuming alarms detect every site problem do not establish safe competence.
